transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Well, what brings me in today is... I've been having this trouble with my eating. Once I start eating those comfort foods, I'll tell myself, 'Maria, that is enough.' But... my hand just still goes back to the pot. It's like I just can’t make myself stop, even when I know I should.
Can you tell me more about those times when you're eating the comfort foods — do you feel like you're not in control of how much you eat, or that you can't stop eating once you start?

Yes, doctor, that's exactly it. Like I was just saying, the control just isn't there. I know in my head that I've had plenty, but I just keep eating anyway. I really just can't seem to stop myself once I get going.
Can you tell me if there are times when you eat a very large amount of food in a short period, like within a couple of hours, more than what most people would eat in that time?

Yes, I do. Some afternoons, usually after I get home from choir or from working out in the garden, I'll fix myself a plate of food... maybe some rice and beans, or a chicken stew. But then I just... I keep going back to the pot for more. In just a short time, I end up eating enough for two or three full meals. So yes, it's definitely a lot more than most folks would eat at one time.
After these times when you eat a large amount, do you ever try to make up for it by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

No, doctor, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up or take any medicine to clear me out, and at my age, I certainly don't go out and exercise extra hard. I just feel bad about it afterwards, but I don't try to get rid of the food.

latest_inference.note: The patient confirmed that she does not engage in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting, laxative use, or excessive exercise after overeating. This rules out bulimia nervosa (F50.2) as the primary diagnosis, leaving binge eating disorder (F50.0) as the most likely.
